problem: Do parks & Indigenous lands inhibit Amazon deforestation and fire?
methods: PRODES-based analysis; fire occurrence; comparison across PA types
findings: Indigenous lands (1/5 of Brazilian Amazon) are the most important barrier to Amazon deforestation; PAs inhibited fire/deforestation
relevance: establishes protection effect of indigenous lands; our study isolates the uncontacted subset

problem: Measuring PA effectiveness avoiding location bias
findings: matched designs reduce estimated PA effectiveness vs naive comparisons
relevance: methodological basis for our matched-control design

problem: Role of Brazilian Amazon PAs in climate mitigation
findings: PAs shelter 54% of remaining forests, 56% of forest carbon; projected avoided emissions
relevance: motivates importance of intact indigenous territories for carbon

journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
problem: Global protected area impacts
findings: PAs reduce clearing ~ (impact smaller than naive estimates)
relevance: supports buffer/matched-comparison logic against remote bias

problem: Does governance regime influence avoided deforestation?
methods: matching; PA types incl. indigenous lands
findings: strictly protected & indigenous lands avoided most deforestation; sustainable-use less
relevance: governance gradient relevant to TI protection stage covariate

problem: Global forest cover change 2000-2012
findings: first global 30 m forest change maps; ~2.3M km2 gross loss 2000-2012
relevance: our primary loss data source (v1.11, 2000-2023)

problem: Roads, deforestation & mitigating effect of PAs
findings: roads are leading deforestation driver; PAs mitigate along roads
relevance: motivates our distance-to-highway covariate

problem: Mortality from contact-related epidemics in Greater Amazonia
findings: median epidemic mortality 18-20%; declining with year/time since contact
relevance: quantifies why no-contact ethics are non-negotiable

problem: Does titling protect forests?
findings: titling reduces clearing >3/4 and disturbance ~2/3 in 2-y window
relevance: titling/regularization stage matters; motivates fase covariate

problem: Global importance of Indigenous lands for conservation
findings: Indigenous peoples manage/have tenure on ~38M km2; overlap w/ biodiversity
relevance: global framing for indigenous land importance

problem: Pervasive rise of small-scale deforestation in Amazonia
methods: satellite time series incl. patches <6.25 ha
findings: 96.4% of new deforestation patches below PRODES 6.25-ha threshold
relevance: justifies GFC (30 m) over PRODES for small clearings near TIPI

problem: BR-319 threat to Amazonian indigenous peoples
findings: highway paving threatens indigenous lands incl. isolated peoples
relevance: documents road threat to TIPI specifically

problem: BR-319 governance failure
findings: lack of governance enables deforestation along road
relevance: supports accessibility-pressure link

problem: Collective property rights & deforestation
findings: full property rights cut deforestation ~66% relative to outside borders
relevance: regularization status as moderator; supports protection effect

problem: Property rights & secondary forest growth
findings: full rights -> less deforestation AND regrowth
relevance: rights -> recovery channel

relevance: latest basin-wide evidence; our study adds the isolated-peoples lens
